raw_english.description: Waiter Curl (Dumbbell) curls both dumbbells from a palms-forward standing position while the elbows stay close to the body.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hold one dumbbell in each hand with palms facing forward.
Keep the upper arms beside the ribs and curl both dumbbells toward the shoulders.
Pause at the top without lifting the elbows.
Lower the dumbbells slowly until the elbows are nearly straight.
raw_english.safety_note: Use dumbbells you can lower without leaning or swinging.

original_dataset_english: Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
Keep your upper arms close to your body and your elbows tucked in.
Slowly curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders, keeping your wrists straight.
Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
user_selected_scene: Single vertical dumbbell near chest, controlled elbow-flexion contraction

Stand tall, feet hip-width apart, upper arms beside ribs; elbows flexed, shoulders relaxed and torso still. ONE dumbbell remains vertical in front of the body with its upper head above its lower head.

Both open palms face upward directly beneath the UPPER dumbbell head, supporting it like a tray. Fingers only stabilize its edges; neither hand grips the central handle. Wrists remain controlled, no ordinary two-dumbbell supinated curl.

Both bare feet planted on floor. Only ONE intact dumbbell with two solid heads and one connecting handle; its lower head hangs below the supported upper head. No bench, cable, second dumbbell or preacher pad.
Flex elbows to bring the vertical dumbbell from lower abdomen/thigh level toward chest, then lower smoothly. Keep elbows near ribs and dumbbell upright; render only the near-chest phase.

raw_english.description: Hold the barbell across the upper back, raise one heel straight up, lower it, then change legs.
instructions: Stand with a barbell across the upper back and one foot planted on the floor.
Keep the other foot off the floor and hold the bar securely.
Raise the planted heel straight up onto the ball of the foot.
Lower the heel to the floor, then switch legs.
form_cues: Keep the ankle over the second toe.
common_mistakes: Pushing off with the other leg.
raw_english.safety_note: Use a handhold or machine support and keep the ankle moving vertically.

/content/en/instructions: Stand with a barbell across the upper back and one foot planted on the floor.

Lower the heel to the floor, then switch legs.
conflicting_catalogue_fields./content/en/safety_note: Use a handhold or machine support and keep the ankle moving vertically.

BOTH hands firmly hold the free bar with a comfortable overhand back-squat grip. Neither hand touches a rack or handhold; no one-handed support while holding the bar.

Low stable nonslip step supports only the right forefoot and permits free heel travel. Select an empty/light free bar for the illustration, no claimed numerical load or plate count. No Smith rails.

Plantarflex the right ankle to raise heel/body, pause and lower slowly under control with ankle tracking vertically. No bouncing, knee-driven lift or pushing with left leg. The user selected step geometry rather than the raw catalogue floor variant.

raw_english.description: A press-under drill moves the body beneath a barbell as it is pressed to a stable overhead position.
instructions: Set the bar at an appropriate height and take a secure overhand grip.
Begin with the bar near the upper chest and brace the trunk.
Press the bar upward while actively moving the body underneath it.
Finish with the bar overhead and elbows locked, then return it to the start.
common_mistakes: Receiving with bent or uneven arms.
raw_english.safety_note: Use an empty bar or light load and a rack with safety supports.

/content/en/instructions: Set the bar at an appropriate height and take a secure overhand grip.

Press the bar upward while actively moving the body underneath it.
Finish with the bar overhead and elbows locked, then return it to the start.

Feet approximately hip-width in a stable bilateral stance; hips and knees flexed only into a QUARTER squat. Trunk braced, free bar stacked overhead, both elbows locked and wrists/elbows/shoulders aligned. No split stance or deep/full overhead squat.
Wide snatch-style overhand grip, one hand on each side of the free bar; even stable lockout.
Both bare feet on floor, empty/light free bar and nearby compatible safety rack without bar-to-rail attachment or hand support. No machine, bench or Smith guide.

User-selected start is bar across upper trapezius BEHIND the neck. raw_english.description: A Back Extension (Machine) uses a supported hip hinge: the torso lowers from the hips and returns only to a neutral line.
instructions: Set the machine so the hips are supported and the feet or legs are secured.
Hinge forward from the hips with a neutral spine and keep the head aligned.
Raise the torso until it is in line with the legs by squeezing the glutes.
Pause briefly, then lower under control without rounding deeply.
common_mistakes: Using the arms to create momentum.
raw_english.safety_note: Stop at a neutral torso line; do not force the machine or bench into hyperextension.

original_dataset_english: Adjust the machine to fit your body size and range of motion.
Sit on the machine with your back against the pad and your feet secured.
Place your hands on the handles or grip bars.
Engage your core and slowly lean forward, allowing your back to round slightly.
Pause for a moment at the bottom position, feeling a stretch in your lower back.
Using your back muscles, slowly raise your torso back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
user_selected_scene: Seated back-extension lever pressed to neutral upright torso

Remain seated with pelvis supported and stabilized, feet braced on fixed platform. Torso has moved from modest forward inclination to neutral upright; head follows spine. No prone hip hinge over a Roman chair and no forced hyperextension.
Hands rest together in front of chest without pulling handles or pushing against the frame; movement is produced by controlled trunk pressure into the rear pad.

raw_english.description: Sit against the dip-machine pad and press the handles down by extending the elbows, then return to the bent-elbow position.
instructions: Adjust the seat height so that your feet are flat on the ground and your knees are at a 90-degree angle.
Grasp the handles of the leverage machine with your palms facing down and your arms fully extended.
Slowly lower your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are parallel to the ground.
Pause for a moment, then push yourself back up to the starting position by straightening your arms.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
form_cues: Track the elbows on the working path.
Stop short of a forced lockout.
raw_english.safety_note: Use a secure back pad or station and stop before the shoulder loses control.

raw_english.description: Sit against the triceps-press pad and extend both elbows along the machine handles before returning to the bent-elbow position.

Start with elbows bent and upper arms close to the torso.

Return the handles until the elbows reach the starting bend.
form_cues: Track the elbows on the working path.
Stop short of a forced lockout.
raw_english.safety_note: Use a secure back pad or station and stop before the shoulder loses control.

raw_english.description: Stand against the shrug-machine pad and elevate the side handles with the shoulders before lowering them.
instructions: Adjust the seat height and position yourself on the leverage machine with your back against the pad.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and keep your arms straight.
Keeping your back straight, lift your shoulders up towards your ears as high as possible.
Hold the contraction for a moment, then slowly lower your shoulders back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
common_mistakes: Using momentum instead of the target joint path.
raw_english.safety_note: Use a secure setup and stop if alignment or control is lost.

raw_english.description: A Belt Squat places the load at the hips so the knees and hips can bend into a squat without a bar resting on the shoulders.
instructions: Secure the belt of the machine around the hips and stand on the platform with a stable stance.
Brace your trunk and bend the knees and hips to lower under control.
Descend to a comfortable depth while keeping the feet planted.
Drive through the platform to stand without locking the knees aggressively.
form_cues: Keep the torso supported by the belt.
raw_english.safety_note: Check the belt and platform connection before loading the machine.

raw_english.description: A machine rear kick extends one hip backward against a pad or lever while the torso stays square.
instructions: Adjust the machine pad and foot or ankle lever for your height.
Brace your hands and torso against the supports and place one leg on the lever.
Drive that leg straight back by extending the hip without arching the spine.
Pause at the end, then return the leg slowly and switch sides.
raw_english.safety_note: Set the machine stop and use a load that keeps the pelvis supported.

user_selected_scene: Standing rear kick with working sole pushing lever footplate backward

Face station with modest forward torso inclination, pelvis square and spine neutral. Left leg bears weight on fixed platform; right knee softly bent and right hip extended backward within controlled range.
Both hands hold fixed handles; forearms/upper torso rest on the prescribed chest/forearm support without twisting.

raw_english.description: A single-leg standing calf raise on the Smith machine lifts one heel while the other foot stays planted on a raised block.
instructions: Set the Smith bar across your upper back, place the ball of one foot on a block, and let the other foot hang clear.
Hold the machine or bar for balance and lower the working heel below the block.
Drive through the ball of the working foot to raise the heel as high as possible.
Pause at the top, then lower slowly and switch legs.
form_cues: Use the full ankle range you can control.
raw_english.safety_note: Use the safety hooks and keep the raised block from sliding.

Place the balls of your feet on a raised surface, such as a weight plate or block.

Hold onto the bar with your hands for stability.
Raise your heels off the ground by extending your ankles, lifting your body up.
Pause at the top of the movement, then slowly lower your heels back down to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

raw_english.description: Bench Press (Cable) is performed supine on a flat bench between low pulleys, pressing one cable handle from each side over the chest.
instructions: Lie flat on the bench with feet planted and one cable handle in each hand.
Start with elbows bent beside the chest and wrists stacked.
Press both handles upward until the arms are straight without letting the shoulders lift.
Lower the handles slowly to the chest and reset.
form_cues: Keep the back on the bench.
common_mistakes: Letting the cables jerk the shoulders back.
raw_english.safety_note: Set both pulleys evenly and keep the cable path clear before pressing.

original_dataset_english: Adjust the cable machine to chest height and attach the handles.
Stand facing away from the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip and step forward to create tension in the cables.
Position your feet firmly on the ground and engage your core.
Bend your elbows and bring your hands to shoulder level, keeping your elbows at a 90-degree angle.
Push the handles forward, extending your arms fully in front of you.
Pause for a moment, then slowly reverse the movement, bringing your hands back to shoulder level.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
user_selected_scene: Supine bilateral cable bench press approaching extension above chest
Lie on FLAT bench, head/back/pelvis supported and both feet planted. Hands above chest, elbows almost straight without forced lockout; shoulders remain controlled against bench.
One D-HANDLE in each hand, closed grip with wrists aligned to forearms. No shared bar or cross-body fly arc.

Flat bench centered between TWO cable towers. Both pulley exits equally LOW, one continuous taut cable from each low side pulley to its own D-handle, clear of bench/body. No standing chest-height press, machine lever or dumbbell substitution.

From bent elbows and hands beside chest, PRESS both handles upward and slightly inward over chest; lower toward chest under control. Elbows flex/extend, not a nearly straight-arm fly. Render the one near-extension phase.
records.scope: Render the user-selected variant only; this is not an independent source confirmation, catalogue correction or PNG acceptance.

raw_english.description: A single-arm cable reverse fly sweeps one handle outward and back in a controlled rear-shoulder arc.
instructions: Set a cable at about shoulder height and stand side-on with the far hand supporting the stance.
Grip the handle with the working arm and hinge slightly at the hips.
Sweep the arm out and back until it aligns with the shoulder without rotating the torso.
Return the handle slowly and switch sides.
raw_english.safety_note: Use a light load and keep the cable path clear of the body.

/content/en/instructions: Set a cable at about shoulder height and stand side-on with the far hand supporting the stance.

raw_english.description: A squat row combines a cable-supported squat with a rope row toward the lower chest.
instructions: Attach the rope to the cable at waist height and stand facing the machine.
Lower into a squat while holding the rope with both hands in a neutral grip.
Stand partway and pull the rope toward the lower chest, driving the elbows back.
Extend the arms and lower into the next squat under control.
form_cues: Keep the chest lifted in the squat.
Pull the rope to the lower chest with elbows back.
common_mistakes: Rowing before the legs begin to extend.
Letting the cable pull the body forward.
raw_english.safety_note: Use a cable load that lets you keep both feet planted while combining the squat and row.

original_dataset_english: Attach a rope to a cable machine at waist height.
Stand facing the cable machine with your feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend your knees and lower your body into a squat position, keeping your back straight and chest up.
Grasp the rope with an overhand grip, with your hands shoulder-width apart.
Engage your core and pull the rope towards your body, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Keep your elbows close to your body and continue pulling until your hands reach your chest.
Pause for a moment at the top of the movement, then slowly release the rope and extend your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
user_selected_scene: Rope row contracted while REMAINING in the squat

Face cable stack, hips/knees held in a stable comfortable squat, chest lifted and back neutral. Both feet planted; elbows drawn back close to ribs and hands near lower ribs/abdomen. Body does NOT rise during the selected row.
One end of ONE rope in each hand, NEUTRAL palms facing each other; closed grips and straight wrists.
LOW pulley in front connected by ONE taut cable to the rope junction. Stand far enough back to keep cable tension, both feet on floor. No waist-height attachment, barbell or rowing seat.

User-selected sequence: squat with arms extended, HOLD squat and row rope to lower ribs/abdomen, re-extend arms while still squatting, THEN stand. Render only contracted row IN squat. Do not blend in the raw partway-standing squat-to-row sequence.
